answer:
Technical intelligence is intelligence concerning foreign technological developments and the performance and operational capabilities of foreign materiel [C1], which now or may eventually have a practical application for military purposes. [C1] It includes all technical aspects of foreign equipment, supplies, installations, facilities, communications, and captured or abandoned items [C1] which have a practical application in furthering military operations. [C1] It also includes technical data of foreign communications equipment [C1] which are derived through communication intelligence, electronic intelligence, and electronic warfare support measures. [C1]

Technical intelligence covers foreign military systems, weapons, weapons systems, and other materiel [C1]; production methods employed in their manufacture [C1]; and related technology pertaining to materiel operation, and logistic support. [C1]

The objectives of technical intelligence that matter most for strategic and tactical planners are to determine foreign technical materiel threats [C2] as they affect strategic and tactical planners and commanders [C2]; determine foreign technological capabilities and limitations [C2]; provide information from which military countermeasures are developed [C2]; provide information which will enable US Forces to use foreign materiel and facilities [C2]; exploit new developments for US military needs [C2]; obtain and exploit items in the DIA Registry, Foreign Materiel Requirements Listing [C2]; provide input on a continuous basis to the overall national integrated S&T intelligence program in consonance with theater policies [C2]; and provide the technical intelligence aspects for tactical and strategic studies on characteristics, capabilities, and limitations of foreign facilities, installations, materiel, and resources. [C2]

It includes all technical aspects of foreign equipment, supplies, installations, facilities, communications, and captured or abandoned items which have a practical application in furthering military operations. Technical intelligence covers foreign military systems, weapons, weapons systems, and other materiel; production methods employed in their manufacture; and related technology pertaining to materiel operation, and logistic support.

The objectives of technical intelligence that matter most for strategic and tactical planners are to determine foreign technical materiel threats as they affect strategic and tactical planners and commanders; determine foreign technological capabilities and limitations; provide information from which military countermeasures are developed; provide information which will enable US Forces to use foreign materiel and facilities; exploit new developments for US military needs; obtain and exploit items in the DIA Registry, Foreign Materiel Requirements Listing; provide input on a continuous basis to the overall national integrated S&T intelligence program in consonance with theater policies; and provide the technical intelligence aspects for tactical and strategic studies on characteristics, capabilities, and limitations of foreign facilities, installations, materiel, and resources.
